name: Marsh (formerly Marsh McLennan)

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (commons file Marsh h rgb c.svg; Marsh brand since Jan 14 2026)

description: Marsh is the largest listed insurance and reinsurance broker by revenue, and it also runs a large consulting arm. Its brokers (Marsh Risk and Guy Carpenter) advise companies on what risks to insure and place the cover with insurers, and are paid mainly by commissions taken out of the premium plus negotiated fees. Mercer sells benefits, pension, investment and career consulting on fees and asset-based charges, and Marsh Management Consulting (Oliver Wyman, Lippincott, NERA) sells project consulting on time and hours. The company also earns interest on premiums and claims money it holds for clients before passing it on. Revenue was $27.0 billion in 2025, of which Risk and Insurance Services was 64% and Consulting 36%.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code 6411 (Insurance Agents, Brokers & Service), from the EDGAR submissions record. The box lumps Marsh with pure brokers, but 36% of revenue is Consulting (Mercer benefits, pension and investment advice; Oliver Wyman strategy consulting), which is paid by fee and does not follow premium cycles.

employees.note: "More than 95,000 colleagues" (FY2025 10-K); about 55,700 in Risk and Insurance Services and 29,100 in Consulting

businessLines.name: Marsh Risk
businessLines.how: Clients (companies, public bodies, individuals) pay through commissions the insurer pays out of the premium, plus fees agreed with the client; insurers also pay for consulting and analytics, administration of programs, and volume-or-profit-based contingent commissions (mainly MMA). Revenue tracks premium rates and the value of what is insured, so it rises with price increases and falls when the P&C market softens; it recurs because programs renew every year.
businessLines.description: Insurance broking and risk advisory for businesses, governments and individuals in 130 countries; includes Marsh McLennan Agency (US mid-market, 135+ agencies acquired since 2009), McGriff (US broker bought Nov 2024 for $7.75B cash), Victor (underwriting manager for specialty programs) and affinity programs.

businessLines.name: Guy Carpenter
businessLines.how: Insurers pay brokerage (commission or fee) when Guy Carpenter places their reinsurance, plus fees for advisory, actuarial and capital-markets structuring work. Revenue follows reinsurance premium volume and pricing.
businessLines.description: Reinsurance intermediary: treaty and facultative broking, catastrophe bonds and other insurance-linked securities (GC Securities), actuarial and analytics.

businessLines.name: Fiduciary interest income (Risk and Insurance Services)
businessLines.how: Float income: brokers collect premiums from clients and hold them briefly before paying insurers, earning interest meanwhile. It rises and falls with short-term interest rates and balances.
businessLines.description: Interest earned on premiums and claims money held on behalf of clients and insurers.

businessLines.name: Mercer
businessLines.how: Employers and pension plans pay consulting fees (time-based or fixed), and investment clients pay a percentage of assets managed or advised, so Wealth revenue moves with markets and asset inflows. Health earns fees and brokerage commissions on employee benefit plans, renewing yearly.
businessLines.description: Health (employer benefits consulting and brokering; outside the US it sells alongside Marsh Risk), Wealth (actuarial, investment consulting and management; about $692B assets managed at Dec 31, 2025) and Career (compensation, engagement and HR advice using proprietary data).

businessLines.name: Marsh Management Consulting
businessLines.how: Corporate and legal clients pay project fees, mostly recognised over time as hours are worked (10-K revenue note); revenue depends on consultant headcount, utilisation and billing rates rather than on insurance prices.
businessLines.description: Oliver Wyman (strategy, risk, finance, AI transformation), Lippincott (brand strategy and design), NERA (economic and legal consulting).
